headline: Run Llama-3 locally in your browser with WebLLM & WebGPU for ultimate health data privacy.
summary: A new approach allows Llama-3 to run entirely client-side using WebLLM and WebGPU, ensuring sensitive health data never leaves your device. This enables 100% private health log analysis.
details: Privacy in HealthTech is a major challenge, but a new tutorial demonstrates how to run Llama-3 entirely client-side. By leveraging WebGPU acceleration and WebLLM, a full Llama-3 instance can operate directly within the browser. This ensures 100% private health log analysis.

This architecture flips the traditional client-server model, keeping all data, the AI model, and computation within the browser's sandbox. This eliminates the risk of sensitive medical logs being used to train corporate models.

The implementation uses WebLLM, a high-performance in-browser LLM inference engine that executes model weights compiled with TVM via the WebGPU API. Specifically, the Llama-3-8B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC variant, optimized for 4-bit quantization, is used to fit browser memory.

For lightweight feature extraction, Transformers.js is integrated to perform Named Entity Recognition (NER), identifying elements like medications or symptoms before Llama-3 handles complex reasoning. The process involves user input, entity extraction, and a clinical summary generated by Llama-3, all on the GPU.

Running Llama-3 in the browser represents a paradigm shift for Edge AI and data privacy. It empowers users with control over their personal health information while still providing the advanced capabilities of large language models.

headline: AI content engine hits 4.6M impressions in 3 months with a new SEO playbook
summary: A new AI-powered SEO playbook, featuring 14 diagnostic scripts and 9 battle-tested configurations, details how one site scaled from 604K to 4.62M monthly impressions in just three months.
details: A new AI-powered content engine playbook reveals the methodology and tools behind a site's growth from 604K to 4.62M monthly impressions in just three months. This system leverages AI agents, Google Search Console (GSC) feedback loops, and automated quality gates.

The methodology is not theoretical prompts but an actual operating system, featuring 14 diagnostic scripts and 9 battle-tested configurations. These include safety guards, agent orchestration, quality gates, and anti-AI detection mechanisms.

The core feedback loop involves GSC data feeding diagnostic scripts to identify issues, which AI agents then fix through quality gates. This iterative process improves rankings and refines the system weekly.

The toolkit includes structured data schemas and CI automation, designed to be replicable. Scripts are standalone Node.js, requiring Google APIs and Google Cloud authentication, with setup guides available for GSC API integration.

The system was developed and refined on ValueAddVC.com, a venture capital content platform. While overall CTR was 0.4% due to AI-overview citations, human-intent CTR improved significantly, with ranked lists hitting 6.8% and question-led posts 3.2%.
